reason: The text explicitly features regular people characters (הָעָם - 'the people', their wives, and various groups) who demonstrate clear agency throughout the passage. Multiple groups speak for themselves, articulating their grievances and circumstances (וְיֵשׁ אֲשֶׁר אֹמְרִים - 'there are some who say'). They respond to Nehemiah's rebuke, agreeing to his proposal (וַיֹּאמְרוּ נָשִׁיב - 'they said we will restore'), and crucially, execute their commitment (וַיַּעַשׂ הָעָם כַּדָּבָר הַזֶּה - 'and the people did according to this word'). The people are active participants who raise concerns, negotiate outcomes, and take action—not passive background figures.
